# White-breasted Swallow

​​​​Blue-and-white Swallow. ygochelidon cyanoleuca​​.

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [University Park](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque)
- [Biotic Inventory](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico)
- White-breasted Swallow

[![Image of a white-breasted swallow](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/45d0dea5-ebe7-4b65-b02b-8c17b8278ad9/web/Pygochelydon-Oyanoleuca.jpg)](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/golondrina-pechiblanca)

![](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/golondrina-pechiblanca)

###### Etymology

Pitangus, Brazilian indigenous name. Sulphuratus, from the Latin sulphuratus, sulfurous.

###### Description

It measures approximately 22 cm. It is one of the largest birds in its family. It lacks sexual dimorphism. The upperparts are dark rufous-brown; the breast and belly are bright yellow; with rufous-edged wings. The head is black, with a nearly hidden bright orange-yellow crest and a white supercilium extending from the base of the bill to the nape; a black crown encircled by a broad white band; a small yellow patch on the cheek; the rest is brown above, with a dark brown iris; a robust black bill; a white throat; a brown tail with rufous margins; and yellow tarsi and toes.

###### Ecology

It is found in human settlements, open areas with scattered trees, tall stubble, along streams and ravine banks; occasionally it may be found in wooded areas, forest edges, secondary forests, and grazing and cultivated areas. Often solitary or in pairs, it is not found in groups. It is a monogamous bird. It builds a large, messy-looking, spherical nest of dry grass with a side entrance in the upper parts of trees: it lays two to four creamy-white eggs with a few reddish-brown spots. It forages at low heights, although it also forages in the canopy. It is an opportunistic bird, feeding on a wide variety of insects and other invertebrates, as well as vertebrates: frogs, lizards, and small mammals; it occasionally eats seeds and fruits and dives to catch fish and tadpoles.

###### Distribution

From South Texas to central Argentina and Trinidad. In Colombia, it is found between 0 and 1500 meters above sea level throughout the country, occasionally at higher altitudes, except in the high mountain ranges, the upper Guajira region, the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the Pacific Coast, and the Sierra de La Macarena. It is one of the most common species along the Aburrá Valley, in parks, gardens, and pasture areas. At EAFIT University, it can be found throughout the campus.
